questions.question: Concerning the cerebellum:

answers.A: It is the largest part of the hind brain
answers.B: It occupies the posterior cranial fossa
answers.C: It is related laterally to the superior sagittal sinus

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the largest hindbrain component and lies in the posterior cranial fossa. The superior sagittal sinus runs in the midline falx cerebri, whereas the transverse sinuses are posterolateral; C is false.

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement:

answers.B: The fibers of the uncrosses pyramidal tract lie in the anterior white matter of the spinal cord

answers.D: The uncrossed pyramidal tract constitutes about 10-20% of the fibers of the original pyramidal tract when it lies in the pyramid

questions.explanation: The corticospinal tract descends mainly in the posterior limb of the internal capsule, not its anterior limb. The lateral and anterior corticospinal tracts and caudal medullary decussation support the other alternatives.

questions.question: Which statement about the spinal cord is false?

answers.B: The lumbosacral enlargement of the spinal cord is called the conus medullaris

questions.explanation: The lumbosacral enlargement is the widened cord region associated with lower-limb innervation; the conus medullaris is the tapered terminal end of the cord. They are distinct structures.

questions.question: The posterior horn of the spinal cord contains the following nuclei except:

questions.explanation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) rootlets emerge from the anterolateral/preolivary sulcus between the pyramid and olive. CN IX, X and XI emerge posterolaterally.

questions.question: The medial lemniscus:

answers.C: Does not cross to the opposite thalamus

questions.explanation: D is the intended best choice, but imprecisely worded: fasciculi gracilis and cuneatus synapse in their medullary nuclei; second-order internal arcuate fibres decussate and form the medial lemniscus, which ascends to the opposite thalamus.
questions.editorial_note: Option D says the lemniscus is formed by gracile and cuneate tracts, which omits the medullary synapse and crossing; review wording before using for assessment.
